Gegenstand des vorliegenden Vergabeverfahrens sind die Leistungen der Objektplanung (Leistungsbild Gebäude und Innenräume) nach § 34 HOAI (Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 2 - 8 sowie bestimmte besondere Leistungen).

title: NASA-White Sand Test Facility-WSTF DEMIL A Mixed Metals Term Contract
description: NASA White Sands Test Facility (WSTF) � DEMIL A Mixed Metals Term Contract Invitation for Bids (IFB): 3-1-QSC-T-27-001 Location: NASA White Sands Test Facility, 12600 NASA Road, Las Cruces, NM 88012 GSA Auctions Listing: https://www.gsaauctions.gov/auctions/preview/380420 IMPORTANT NOTICE: This auction requires the apparent high bidder to submit completed and signed certification(s) found in the "Documents" section and/or proof of licensing to the Sales Contracting Officer before the award is finalized. Requirements vary by auction. Property Description This Invitation for Bids (IFB) is for a Comprehensive Scrap Metal Collection, Removal, and Recycling Services Sale Term Contract at NASA White Sands Test Facility. The estimated annual quantity is 130 tons of mixed, unsegregated, and unprepared scrap iron and steel, including light and heavy steel. Scrap may contain ferrous and nonferrous attachments and other foreign materials. Submission of Bids Required Email Subject: Bid Submission for 3-1-QSC-T-27-001 (TC) Email Bid Submissions To: westzonesealedbids@gsa.gov Important Solicitation Dates IFB Issuance Date: 15 October 2026 Deadline for Questions: 09 November 2026 Bid Submission Deadline: 13 November 2026 � 5:00 PM Central Time Bid Opening: 17 November 2026 � 11:00 AM Central Time Anticipated Pre-Award Date: 20 November 2026 KEY REQUIREMENTS (READ CAREFULLY) MANDATORY Pre-Bid Site Inspection Required (See IFB Section 3.3). Bid submissions must include completed Appendix A and Standard Form 114 (SF 114). Performance Guarantee Required: $6,000.00. Pricing is based on a percentage of a published market index. The contractor shall furnish required insurance documentation prior to performance in accordance with IFB Section 7.2. All solicitation amendments must be acknowledged, if applicable. Failure to comply with applicable solicitation requirements may result in a bid being deemed nonresponsive. Mandatory Pre-Bid Site Inspection (IFB Section 3.3) SITE ACCESS / SECURITY NASA White Sands Test Facility is a secured Federal installation. Advance coordination is required for all site access. Badging and access controls apply, and additional security restrictions may be enforced. All mandatory pre-bid site inspections must be scheduled and coordinated with the Government representatives identified below. Site Points of Contact (POCs): Pedro "Pete" Rios Email: pete.rios-1@nasa.gov Mobile: 575-779-6149 Office: 575-524-5138 Johnny J. Bernal Email: johnny.j.bernal@nasa.gov Mobile: 575-649-5284 Office: 575-524-5140 Solicitation Documents and Questions All solicitation documents, including the IFB, Surveillance Plan, and Appendices, are available in the Documents section of the GSA Auctions listing: https://www.gsaauctions.gov/auctions/preview/380420 Prospective bidders are responsible for reviewing the complete IFB, all applicable attachments, and any amendments before submitting a bid. All questions must be submitted in writing before the deadline identified in the IFB. Email Bid Questions To: alfonso.brown@gsa.gov Sales Contracting Officer (SCO) Alfonso L. Brown Sr. General Services Administration (GSA) Email: alfonso.brown@gsa.gov Phone: 817-978-0771

title: Czechia – Construction work – Realizace protipovodňových opatření města Brna - Etapy IX,X,XI – výběr zhotovitele
description: Předmětem zadávacího řízení je uzavření smlouvy o dílo dle Smluvních podmínek pro výstavbu pozemních a inženýrských sítí staveb projektovaných objednatelem dle FIDIC RED BOOK, 1. vydání, 1999, vydaných v českém překladu Českou asociací konzultačních inženýrů (CACE) v roce 2017, a dalších dokumentů tvořících smlouvu o dílo. Předmětem plnění Veřejné zakázky jsou stavební práce v rámci realizace Díla zahrnující zejména činnosti dle odst. 4.2.4 Zadávací dokumentace. Kompletní seznam realizovaných stavebních objektů v rámci Veřejné zakázky je uveden v příloze č. 7 ZD. Dílo je děleno na následující Sekce: a) Sekce 1 – Stavební objekty přeložek; b) Sekce 2 – Stavební objekty zařazené do projektu – Způsobilé výdaje; c) Sekce 3 – Stavební objekty zařazené do projektu – Nezpůsobilé výdaje; d) Sekce 4 – Stavební objekty zařazené mimo projekt, (v podrobnostech k jednotlivým Sekcím viz příloha č. 7 ZD /Technická specifikace/). Dodavatel bude provádět stavební práce při realizaci Díla, konkrétně se jedná o výstavbu protipovodňových opatření, a to včetně provedení souvisejících terénních a krajinných úprav, a to za podmínek dále specifikovaných ve Smlouvě.

title: Base and Medical Laundry Services -Qatar and Saudi Arabia
description: Sources Sought Laundry and Dry-Cleaning Services THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. The 379th Contracting Squadron is conducting market research to determine interest and capability of potential sources. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. The 379th Contracting Squadron is seeking potential sources for the purchase of Laundry and Dry-Cleaning services in the Qatar and Saudi Arabia regions. Please see Attachments 1, 2 and 3 for complete list of areas to be covered. The recommended North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 812320 - Cleaners, drycleaning and laundry service (except coin-operated) with a size standard of $8M. � If there is a NAICS code that you believe would be more applicable, please provide with your capability statement. Please accompany your capability statement with answers to the following questions: 1. Are you able to provide all the services listed in the requirement? Do you anticipate any challenges? If so, what are they? 2. If it is required to conduct a site visit prior to contract award, approximately how many business days would it take your company to prepare the site for a visit by government representatives? 3. Do you have experience handling and cleaning contaminated medical linen? If so, to whom and for how long? Describe your experience adhering to regulations for handling and cleaning medical linen. 4. Do you have dedicated equipment and processes for handling contaminated medical linen separately from other laundry? Describe the segregation process. 5. Describe your quality control procedures to ensure that linen is thoroughly cleaned, disinfected, and free of damage. 6. Describe your transportation methods for both soiled and clean linen and how often do you sanitize your transport vehicles? 7. Are you able to handle specialized cleaning needs, such as stain removal or repairs? 8. Do you have a system for monitoring and controlling water temperature and chemical concentrations during the washing process? 9. Do you intend to provide a quote for this requirement? How many days would you need to draft a quote? Provide any additional questions or comments related to the requirement. All responses will be posted. This Sources Sought Announcement is solely for informational and planning purposes only and is not a solicitation or Request for Quote. Please send responses to: SrA Dominique Henry, Contracting Officer, Dominique.henry.1@us.af.mil no later than 12:00PM Arabian Standard Time on 14 November, 2025.

description: ΔΙΑΚΗΡΥΞΗ: 70η/2026 ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΟΥ ΔΙΕΘΝΟΥΣ ΑΝΟΙΚΤΟΥ ΔΙΑΓΩΝΙΣΜΟΥ ΑΝΩ ΤΩΝ ΟΡΙΩΝ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΠΡΟΜΗΘΕΙΑ «Καυσίμων», δηλαδή : Εκτιμώμενος Προϋπολογισμός για ένα έτος (12 μήνες): 645.158,35 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ ή 799.996,36 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου Φ.Π.Α 24%. Αναλυτικά για ένα έτος; Προϋπολογισμός Πετρελαίου Θέρμανσης CPV:09135100-5 : 580.122,58 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ ή 719.352,00 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου Φ.Π.Α 24%, Προϋπολογισμός Πετρελαίου Κίνησης CPV:09134100-8: 63.428,52 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ ή 78.651,36 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου Φ.Π.Α 24%, Προϋπολογισμός Βενζίνης Αμόλυβδης 95 Οκτανίων CPV:09132100-4: 1.607,26 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ ή 1.993,00 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου Φ.Π.Α 24%, Και με δικαίωμα προαίρεσης για ακόμη ένα έτος με τους ίδιους όρους και το ίδιο ποσό Εκτιμώμενος Συνολικός Προϋπολογισμός : 1.290.316,71 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ ή 1.599.992,72 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου Φ.Π.Α 24%. Πετρελαίου Θέρμανσης CPV:09135100-5, για την κάλυψη των αναγκών του Γενικού Νοσοκομείου Χαλκιδικής, του Ψυχιατρικού Ξενώνα, της Μονάδας Τεχνητού Νεφρού και του ΚΕ.Φ.ΙΑ.Π, Πετρελαίου Κίνησης CPV:09134100-8 για την γεννήτρια παροχής ρεύματος, για κάλυψη διαφόρων αναγκών θέρμανσης ( σε περιόδους μη διάθεσης πετρελαίου Θέρμανσης ) αλλά και για την κίνηση των οχημάτων και Βενζίνης Αμόλυβδης 95 Οκτανίων CPV:09132100-4 για την κίνηση των οχημάτων του Νοσοκομείου και του ΚΕ.Φ.ΙΑ.Π, χρονικής διάρκειας ενός έτους (12 μήνες) με δικαίωμα προαίρεσης για ακόμη ένα έτος με τους ίδιους όρους και το ίδιο ποσό. Κριτήριο ανάθεσης της Σύμβασης είναι η πλέον συμφέρουσα από οικονομική άποψη προσφορά, αποκλειστικά βάση της τιμής ανά τμήμα, η οποία θα δοθεί ως εξής (βάση του άρθρου 95 του Ν.4412/2016) δηλαδή :  το μεγαλύτερο ποσοστό έκπτωσης επί τοις εκατό (%) επί της εκάστοτε διαμορφούμενης, μέσης λιανικής τιμής πώλησης έκαστου είδους, του Παρατηρητηρίου Τιμών Υγρών Καυσίμων του Υπουργείου Ανάπτυξης για τον Νομό Χαλκιδικής (http://www.fuelprices.gr), κατά την ημέρα παράδοσης αυτού και που θα αντιστοιχεί σε κάθε χαρακτηριστικό γνώρισμα του είδους (πετρέλαιο θέρμανσης, πετρέλαιο κίνησης και βενζίνη αμόλυβδη).

title: Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) 2026 Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) seeks innovative approaches to address challenges related to quantum computing. The Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) aims to examine approaches for constructing a utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer and computational workflows that include quantum compute steps. Proposed research should investigate approaches that enable revolutionary advances in design, engineering, test, and evaluation of such systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. To rapidly capitalize on new opportunities, DARPA announces the QBI 2026 opportunity, which seeks specific solutions to targeted challenges related to developing utility-scale quantum computers, as defined in specific QBI topic (QBIT) calls. Each QBIT will (1) outline specific details regarding the research topic of interest and (2) provide proposal and submission instructions, including the due date for proposal submission, in addition to those outlined in this PA. Proposals must only be submitted in response to a QBIT. Proposals submitted directly to this PA will not be considered.

Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency s Needs: VA OGC has a new requirement for expert witness litigation support services from XXXX XXXXXX, of LitCon Group, LLC in support of ongoing litigation of CBCA Claims 7718, 8054 and 8056, Alexander CPA, PLLC v Department of Veterans Affairs. The expert witness shall perform the following services: Review and analyze the Appellant's expert report(s) and the supporting data, methodologies, and assumptions relied upon, including any damages model and any opinions concerning industry-standard practices; Review relevant contract documentation, including the contract and its Performance Work Statement, the contingency-fee payment structure, the task order/ordering mechanism, the Feasibility Assessment Report requirements, claim denial and compliant-payment data, and applicable correspondence and administrative record materials provided by VA counsel; Evaluate the reliability and validity of the opposing expert's damages calculations, including the reasonableness of recovery projections derived from collected/closed claim populations, treatment of the contingency-fee model, assumptions regarding recoverable amounts, causation linking alleged VA conduct to claimed losses, and any failure to account for contract terms limiting or conditioning recovery (e.g., task-order issuance contingent on feasibility results, exclusions of certain claim categories, refund-request offsets, and cessation of payment six months after task order expiration); Prepare a written rebuttal report stating the expert's opinions, the bases and reasons for them, the facts and data considered, and the expert's qualifications, consistent with the standards applicable to expert reports before the CBCA; Provide deposition and hearing testimony as required and prepare for such testimony; Assist with VA s preparation for the deposition of Appellant s expert and assistance with VA s trial preparation; Assist with VA s preparation for, and attendance at, ADR, should one be conducted; and Consult with VA counsel throughout the engagement and respond to follow-up analytical requests as needed. description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. title: High-Capacity Hydrogen and Hydrogen Isotope Getters
description: Even small amounts of hydrogen can damage sensitive equipment over time. As hydrogen accumulates inside sealed environments, it can corrode metals, weaken structural materials, degrade electronic components, and, in some applications, create explosion hazards. Preventing that buildup is essential for maintaining the reliability and safety of many high-value systems. Hydrogen getters are materials built into sealed devices and systems to remove hydrogen before it can accumulate. Like a moisture absorber, they remove an unwanted gas. Instead of trapping water, however, they chemically react with hydrogen and lock it away permanently. Depending on the application, a getter may take the form of a pellet, coating, thin film, powder, or printable material. Many commercially available getters rely on zirconium-based materials that offer limited hydrogen storage capacity, require activation before use, or operate effectively only within a narrow temperature range. Some also depend on costly vacuum-deposition manufacturing processes that limit design flexibility. Los Alamos researchers have developed a new class of hydrogen getters designed to overcome these limitations. The materials capture hydrogen and its isotopes, including deuterium and tritium, across a broad range of operating conditions without requiring activation while offering significantly higher storage capacity and greater flexibility for manufacturing and product integration. Value Proposition Hydrogen can quietly build up inside sealed devices and industrial systems, shortening equipment life and creating safety risks. Los Alamos National Laboratory has developed a new class of high-capacity hydrogen getters that permanently remove hydrogen before it causes damage. Compared with conventional getters, this technology stores more hydrogen, operates across a wider range of conditions, and can be manufactured in multiple forms for easy integration into commercial products. Hydrogen uptake rate decreases as getter materials fill with hydrogen. Compared with a conventional getter (brown), the LANL high-capacity getter (green) maintains rapid hydrogen capture over a much larger storage capacity. Advantages Stores significantly more hydrogen than many conventional getter materials. Permanently removes hydrogen, improving long-term reliability in sealed systems. Operates across a broad temperature range without activation. Captures hydrogen even at pressures well below atmospheric levels. Selectively removes hydrogen in mixed-gas environments. Hydrogen uptake rates can be tailored to specific applications. Compatible with polymers and available as films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, and printable pastes for flexible product integration. Reduces projected material and manufacturing costs compared with many zirconium-based getter technologies. Scalable manufacturing supports applications ranging from miniature electronics to large industrial systems. Technology Description The getter materials chemically react with hydrogen and its isotopes to form stable compounds that permanently lock the hydrogen inside the material, providing long-term protection for sealed devices and industrial equipment. The technology is based on a novel organic alkyne chemistry. Alkynes are carbon-containing molecules that readily react with hydrogen, allowing the material to store substantially more hydrogen than many conventional getter systems. Unlike many commercial getters, these materials operate without activation and continue to perform across a broad temperature range. They also selectively capture hydrogen in the presence of gases such as helium, nitrogen, argon, and methane, making them well suited for complex industrial and vacuum environments. The hydrogen capture rate can be tailored by adjusting the catalyst formulation for specific operating conditions. Hydrogen capture has also been demonstrated at pressures well below atmospheric conditions, expanding the range of potential applications. The materials are compatible with polymers and other common manufacturing materials, allowing them to be incorporated into films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, adhesives, foams, and printable pastes. Market Applications Semiconductor and microelectronics packaging Hermetically sealed electronics Aerospace and defense Medical devices Nuclear material storage and processing Vacuum and gas purification systems Cryogenic equipment Oil and gas infrastructure Scientific instrumentation High-reliability industrial systems TRL 4 U.S. patent pending LA-UR-26-25730 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Sacramento District (SPK), anticipates solicitation of a requirement for design-build (DB) and design-bid-build (DBB) � Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Construction Services in support of SPK�s Military Boundary and Area of Responsibility. Specific needs will be determined based upon project requirements as described in each task order. Selected firms will work on a variety of projects that may include but not necessarily limited to new construction (including new work, additions, alterations, maintenance, and repairs) of commercial and institutional buildings and related structures. Anticipated work may include the following: new construction, additions, alterations, renovations, repairs, and maintenance of facilities and supporting infrastructure. The Government anticipates establishing a MATOC with a total shared capacity of $465,000,000 with an 8-year ordering period (five-year base with one three-year option period). The Government intends to award up to seven (7) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. However, The Government reserves the right to award more or fewer than 7 IDIQ contracts if it is determined to be in the best interest of the government. The MATOC will primarily support Military, IIS, DVA, and Civil Works projects for Sacramento District (SPK). The Government currently estimates the magnitude of construction for the task orders to be between $2,500.00 and $20,000,000.00. Contractors will be required to maintain sufficient bonding to cover the value of all awarded task orders. title: JP Martha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit
description: JP Martha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. description: THIS IS NOT AN INVITIATION FOR BID, PLAN AND SPEFICIATIONS ARE NOT AVAILBLE PROJECT NAME: HI FLAP CR562(1) Kilauea Point PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Kilauea Point National Wildlife Refuge (KPNWR) is a 203-acre facility located on the north shore of the Island of Kaua'i. It is part of the Kaua'i National Wildlife Refuge Complex managed by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service. To keep up with the visitation demands, the KPNWR and the USFWS along with the Federal Highway Administration Central Federal Lands Highway Division is proposing to improve the area by providing better access along Kolo Road and Kilauea Road (Route 562) for pedestrians and bicyclists, as well as improvements to the overlook. The project consists of installation of a sidewalk adjacent the existing roadway from the intersection of Kuhio Highway to the KPNWR Overlook. Work includes pavement rehabilitation and resurfacing of the existing roadway, with full depth pavement on aggregate base course for roadway widening segments, and reconstruction of the existing turnaround. Guardrail, sidewalk, curb, gutter, two mini-roundabouts, striping, and pedestrian crossings will be provided to establish a safe and accessible corridor for pedestrians and bicyclists. Minor utility adjustments and construction is also anticipated. The total project length is approximately 1.70 miles. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: 18,500 square yards of Removal of Pavement, Asphalt 3,370 cubic yards of Roadway Excavation 2,900 ton of Roadway Aggregate, Method 2 4,200 ton of Asphalt Concrete pavement, Type 1 630 square yard of minor concrete Pavement, Reinforced 1,540 linear feet of Curb, Concrete, 16-Inch Depth (Slotted) 5,670 square yards of Sidewalk, Concrete 34 Accessibility Ramps, Concrete ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertise: End of October or Early November 2026 Bid Opening: December 2026 Award: January 2027 Construction: January 2027 �January 2028 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: The anticipated cost range is between 10,000,000 and $20,000,000.

description: L'enquête suisse sur la population active (ESPA) est une enquête auprès des personnes qui est réalisée chaque année depuis 1991. Le but principal de l'ESPA est de fournir des données sur la structure de la population active et sur les comportements en matière d'activité professionnelle. Grâce à l'application stricte de définitions internationales, les données de la Suisse peuvent être comparées avec celles des pays de l'OCDE et de l'Union européenne. Depuis 2010, l'ESPA se déroule en continu. Enquête suisse sur la population active (ESPA) | Office fédéral de la statistique - OFS <https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/fr/home/statistiques/travail-remuneration/enquetes/espa.html> L'appel d'offres porte sur les prestations suivantes : - Mise en œuvre l'ESPA en multimode (CAWI et CATI) selon les spécifications du « responsive web design », sur la base d'un questionnaire fourni par l’OFS. Cela comprend la mise en œuvre des thèmes supplémentaires, la préparation (notamment la programmation), la réalisation (y compris la gestion des adresses et une hotline téléphonique), le monitoring, l'évaluation et le traitement des résultats des entretiens pour les années suivantes : > 2027 : Préparation et réalisation des enquêtes pilotes ESPA en mixed mode, y compris la gestion des adresses, la hotline téléphonique et l'analyse des enquêtes pilotes. > 2028 : Réalisation de l'ESPA pour une partie de l'échantillon, sans modules thématiques > 2029 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 2 modules thématiques > 2030 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 2 modules thématiques > 2031 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 1 à 2 modules thématiques > 2032 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 2 modules thématiques > 2033 : Répétition de l'ESPA pour une partie de l'échantillon (complétude des vagues), y compris 1 à 2 modules thématiques > 2034 : Répétition de l'ESPA pour une partie de l'échantillon (complétude des vagues), sans modules thématiques - Préparation, réalisation et évaluation de prétests CATI pour les années 2028 à 2032

description: Gävle kommun har idag två separata avtal avseende arbetskläder (yrkes-, varsel-, skydds- och flamskyddande kläder) samt arbetsskor, där totalt fyra (4) Leverantörer är antagna, två (2) Leverantörer per avtal. Avtalen är fördelade enligt följande: Avtal 1: Arbetskläder för kost, lokalvård och omvårdnad Avtal 2: Yrkes-, varsel-, skydds- och flamskyddande arbetskläder Inför kommande upphandling har Gävle kommun valt att tillgodose huvuddelen av behovet av arbetskläder inom vård- och omsorgsverksamheten genom ett separat avtal för hyrda arbetskläder inklusive cirkulationstvätt. Detta innebär att behovet av att köpa arbetskläder för dessa verksamheter kommer att minska väsentligt. Därutöver har de tidigare avtalen omfattat ett sortiment med i stor utsträckning likvärdiga produkter. Mot denna bakgrund bedömer Beställaren att det inte längre finns ett behov av att teckna avtal med flera Leverantörer. Avtal kommer därför att tecknas med en (1) Leverantör. En ensam Leverantör bedöms ge verksamheterna en enklare beställningsprocess, minska den administrativa hanteringen samt skapa bättre förutsättningar för en effektiv avtalsförvaltning, uppföljning och utveckling av avtalet under avtalsperioden.

title: Digitalt stoffkartotek

title: Military Recruiting Lease for office space 5,300 to 5,800 SF required
description: The Honolulu District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is soliciting lease proposals for 5,300 to 5,800 of gross rentable square feet of office and related space in Honolulu, Hawaii for Armed Forces Recruiting purposes. The U.S. Government, by and through USACE, currently occupies office and related space under a lease, in the city and state specified above. The Lessor shall provide adequate/assigned parking for approximately twelve (12) Government vehicles both during the day and overnight. The lease term is four (4) years eleven (11) months with Government termination rights and will be a full-service lease (to include all utilities and janitorial services). Delineated area: The Government requests Space in Honolulu, Hawaii in an area bounded as follows: North: River St. South: Ward Ave. East: Ala Moana Blvd. West: S. Vinyard Blvd. Buildings that have frontage on the boundary streets are deemed to be within the Delineated Area. If awarded to a new location, this office would be relocated immediately upon completion of construction to accommodate all requirements pertaining to the FY26 Construction Specifications for TAOC Offices with the lease start date commencing upon acceptance of space by the government (see attached construction specifications). Space Minimum requirements include: 1. 24-hour unrestricted access to Leased space; 2. Availability of all communications infrastructure for to include DSL, T1 or a satellite dish; 3. Direct access to secondary exterior exit door from Lease space; common area exterior exit door if shared with other military services; or exterior exit door can, and will be installed prior to occupying the facility; and 4. 24-hour lighted parking for up to twelve (12) Government vehicles and adequate parking for privately owned vehicles onsite or within a 4 block radius of the premises. Electronic Offer Submission: Offers must be submitted electronically via email to: amy.capwell@usace.army.mil Offers are due on or before: November 15, 2026. Any questions regarding this solicitation may be directed to the Primary Point of Contact listed in the �Contact Information� section of this notice. To be responsive, your offer should be based on all the terms, conditions, and responsibilities expressed throughout the RLP and Lease. Please review the RLP and all attachments carefully paying particular attention to the solicitation requirements. The requirements for consideration of award will entail a complete bid that consists of the following criteria at a minimum: (Note: There may be other required forms. Refer to the enclosed RLP for details.): Initialed acceptance and use of government Lease indicating that you understand the Government�s terms and requirements. (Exhibit A Recruiting Form L100) 2. Initialed acceptance and use of government General Clauses Form 3517B indicating that you understand the Government�s terms and requirements. (Exhibit B Form 3517B General Clauses) 3. Competitive rates of base cost per square feet for annual rent and a breakout of operating expenses, Real Estate Taxes, and Janitorial service costs and Utilities. (Completed Exhibit C Proposal to Lease). 4. All costs and materials affiliated to meet the requirements of the construction specifications including all safety and security enhancements will be considered Tenant Improvements with no reimbursement from the government upon completion of the construction or through amortization within the Lease (Completed Exhibit F Construction Bid Worksheet). Do not attempt to complete the Lease form (USACE Recruiting Lease Form L100). Neither the RLP nor any other part of an Offeror�s proposal shall be part of the Lease except to the extent expressly incorporated therein. Please review all the documents thoroughly so that you have a complete understanding of the Government�s requirements. After receipt of all proposals, conclusions of any discussions, and receipt of best and final offers, the Government will select a location based on the lowest overall cost and technical requirements specified in the enclosed RLP. Past performance, if applicable, will also be taken into consideration. The selection is expected to occur approximately thirty (30) days following the initial proposal response date. A Government market survey, appraisal, or value estimate will be conducted to determine fair market rental value. One item of note in the General Clauses, GSA Form 3517B document is the requirement to register in the System for Award Management at www.SAM.gov (General Clause 17, CFR 52.204-7). This registration is mandatory for any entity wishing to do business with the Government and must be completed before lease award. NOTICE: The following information is provided for situational awareness and is not required to respond to this Sources Sought. All contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) prior to award of a contract. All proposed contractors are highly encouraged to review FAR Clause 52.232-33 Payments by Electronic Funds Transfer � System for Award Management, which indicates �All payments by the Government under this contract shall be made by electronic funds transfer (EFT).� Those not currently registered can obtain registration by going to the website http://www.SAM.gov. The process can usually be completed from 24 to 48 hours after submission. Contractors will need to obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS number) for processing their registration. If you do not already have a Unique Entity Identifier, one can be obtained from http://www.SAM.gov. Refer to www.SAM.gov for information formerly found in CCR, EPLS, ORCA and FedReg. Please begin the registration process immediately in order to avoid delay of the contract award should your firm be selected. ALERT: You must submit a notarized letter appointing the authorized Entity Administrator before your registration will be activated. This requirement now applies to both new and existing entities. Effective 29 April 2018, the notarized letter process is now mandatory on all CURRENT registrants at SAM who have a requirement to update data on their SAM record. The notarized letter is mandatory and is required before the GSA Federal Service Desk (FSD) will activate the entity's registration. Effective 29 June 2018, vendors creating or updating their registration can have their registration activated prior to the approval of the required notarized letter. However, the signed copy of the notarized letter must be sent to the GSA Federal Service Desk (FSD) within 30 days of activation or the vendor risks no longer being active in SAM. Vendors can check whether an account is active by performing a query by their CAGE or Unique Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS number). The new registration process may now take several weeks, so vendors are highly encouraged to begin registering as soon as possible to avoid any possible delays in future contract awards. Remember, there is no cost to use SAM. To find out additional information about the changes of the SAM registration process, contractors should visit the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) link located at the top of the SAM homepage (www.sam.gov). Funds may or may not be presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds are available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date for receipt of proposals. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse offeror(s) for any cost.

title: Greece, Lithuania, Poland, Cyprus – Research and experimental development services – Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP)
description: The Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP) project addresses critical gaps in personal protective equipment (PPE). It responds to the need to keep first responders safe and operationally effective during evolving threats, from CBRN incidents and HAZMAT situations to terrorism, industrial accidents, natural disasters, and other complex emergencies. ACTIVE PCP involves public safety buyers and end-users in defining unmet needs and guiding industry R&D towards solutions. ACTIVE PCP procures R&D services through Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP). // Tenderers are invited to propose innovative PPE solutions for first responders, police, firefighters, and emergency medical services operating in complex CBRN and HAZMAT environments. Following the phased PCP model, the procurement supports R&D up to the development of a limited volume of first products. It comprises 3 competitive Phases, with fewer Tenderers progressing at each stage so that those offering the strongest response to the PCP's technical challenge are selected. // The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement (FA) with call-offs for specific contracts for each of the 3 R&D phases (altogether ‘Contracts’). Greek law governs the Contracts. The GDPR Processing Agreement – if applicable – will be governed by the law of the Member State in which each pilot will take place during Phase 3. The FA will remain binding for the duration of all phases for which Contractors remain in the PCP. There will be no renegotiations. // KEMEA will be the Lead Procurer throughout all the phases of ACTIVE PCP. // Tenderers that are awarded a FA will also be awarded a specific contract for Phase 1 (evaluation of tenders for the FA and Phase 1 are combined). Tenderers are therefore asked not only to submit their detailed offer for Phase 1, but also to state their goals, and to outline their plans (including price conditions) for Phases 2 and 3. // The three Phases are: (i) Phase 1: Solution Design. A FA and a Specific Contract for Phase 1 will be awarded to at least six (6) contractors; (ii) Phase 2: Prototyping. A call-off will be organised for Phase 2, with the aim of awarding at least three (3) Phase 2 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 1 will be eligible for Phase 2. The procurers will validate the Phase 2 prototypes; and (iii) Phase 3: Original development and testing. A second call-off will be organised for Phase 3, with the aim of awarding a minimum of two (2) Phase 3 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 2 will be eligible for Phase 3. The procurers will validate the Phase 3 prototypes. // Offers for the next phase will be requested together with the End of Phase deliverables of the previous phase. I.e., all Contractors of the previous phase have the right to submit offers for the next phase (together with their End of Phase Report). A Contractor must have been awarded a Specific Contract for Phase 1 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 2. Likewise, a Contractor must have been awarded Specific Contracts for Phases 1 and 2 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 3. The maximum total budget for this PCP is 3.650.000 EUR including VAT, taxes and other related fees and costs). // The maximum budget per phase and the maximum budget per Contractor (excluding VAT, including taxes and other related fees and costs) are as follows: For Phase 1 (Solution Design): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €47,043.00; Total subcontracting cost for phase 1: €282,258.05. For Phase 2 (Prototyping): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €483,870.97; Total subcontracting cost for phase 2: €1,451,612.90. For Phase 3 (Original development and testing): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €604,838.71; Total subcontracting cost for phase 3: €1,209,677.42. For Phase 1, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of Tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 2, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best Tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 3, contracts for Phase 3 will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // As leftover budget from the previous phase can be transferred to the next phase(s), the total budget available for Phases 2 and/or 3 may eventually be higher than stated here (but the maximum budget per Contractor for Phases 2 and 3 will remain the same). // Further information on ACTIVE PCP as well as the Tender Documents can be found at https://www.activepcp.eu/

description: Kajaanin ammattikorkeakoulun 3D-mittaus- ja skannausjärjestelmän hankinta opetus-, tutkimus- ja yritysyhteistyökäyttöön Hankinnan kohteena on 3D-mittaus- ja skannausjärjestelmä, joka koostuu kannettavasta 3D käsiskannerista, mittakäsivarresta sekä niiden käyttöön tarvittavista ohjelmistoista, koulutuksesta ja tukipalveluista. title: SPECIAL MISSIONS TRAINING CENTER LIVE-FIRE MARITIME/URBAN TRAINING SYSTEM
description: Purpose: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for market-research purposes to identify capable sources; available commercial solutions; current industry practices; potential acquisition approaches; and relevant technical, schedule, lifecycle-support, and cost information for the design, engineering, fabrication, delivery, installation, integration, testing, certification/validation, and commissioning of a Joint Maritime Training Facility (JMTF) live-fire maritime/urban training system. Site Visit Location: Participants are requested to assemble at The Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune Provost Marshal�s Office is located in Building 58 on Virginia Dare Drive, Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. Date: November 10, 2026 The contemplated requirement is for a complete and operational live-fire training system at the USCG Special Missions Training Center (SMTC), Courthouse Bay, Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. The facility must support realistic, modular, multi-level tactical training, including maritime interdiction, close-quarters combat, vertical access, breaching, and related joint-service mission sets. The system must integrate ballistic containment with maritime and urban training features and be suitable for repeated use in an outdoor coastal environment. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 236220. Disclaimer: There is no solicitation at this time. This RFI is not a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this request is purely voluntary; the Government will not pay for any costs incurred nor is obligated to respond. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. After reviewing RFI responses to this RFI, and if the USCG still plans to proceed with the acquisition, a solicitation announcement may be published on the Contract Opportunities (formerly FedBizOpps) website or distributed to contract holders if a strategically-sourced vehicle is deemed appropriate. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor the Contract Opportunities website. Failure to respond or submit sufficiently detailed information may result in a company not being considered a likely offeror when making a decision on whether or how to set aside a solicitation for restricted competition. Regardless of the information submitted, the Government reserves the right to consider any arrangement as determined appropriate for this requirement. No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response to this RFI. The Government reserves the right to use any information provided by respondents for any purpose determined necessary and legally appropriate, including using technical information provided by respondents in any resultant solicitation. The anticipated contractor would provide all labor, supervision, project management, engineering, materials, equipment, transportation, installation, testing, documentation, commissioning, and training necessary to deliver a complete live-fire maritime/urban training facility. The anticipated effort includes: Complete facility design and engineering, including ballistic, structural, civil, architectural, mechanical, electrical, fire/life-safety, safety, and training-system interfaces. Preparation of a Design Basis Report; design packages; calculations; submittals; shop and fabrication drawings; installation plans; final as-built drawings; and operations and maintenance (O&M) manuals. Fabrication, delivery, installation, integration, testing, ballistic certification or validation, commissioning, and Government acceptance support. A ballistic wall and containment system rated and validated for the Government-approved firing geometry, engagement distances, and training conditions, with a planning threat basis of 6.8 mm XM1188E1 ammunition, with an additional 12-inch layer of sacrificial ballistic rubber blocks or an appropriate bullet-trap target system. Projectile-management and ricochet-mitigation surfacing; reconfigurable ballistic panels; and portable bullet traps. A multi-level training system incorporating urban, maritime, and lower-deck training areas; configurable rooms and corridors; ship-type doors and hatches; ladders; grated decks; confined passageways; vertical-access/rappelling features; observation catwalks; and instructor viewing platforms. Foundations, slabs, structural framing, site preparation, drainage, lighting, electrical distribution, ventilation/air exchange, weather protection, fire detection/alarm components, emergency egress, and other systems required for the approved design. Corrosion resistance and weather protection appropriate for a coastal Camp Lejeune environment. Operator/instructor training, maintenance training, recommended spare-parts lists, inspection checklists, maintenance schedules, and lifecycle-support recommendations. Project management, recurring coordination meetings, progress reporting, integrated scheduling, and coordination with Camp Lejeune access, safety, security, delivery, and range-operation requirements. title: Cost Effective On-Base Parcel Delivery Solutions (RAFL, RAFM, RAFF, United Kingdom)
description: The 48th Contracting Squadron at Royal Air Force (RAF) Lakenheath, United Kingdom, seeks to identify qualified sources and cost-effective commercially practical solutions capable of providing reliable on-base parcel delivery services for RAF Lakenheath (RAFL), RAF Mildenhall (RAFM), and RAF Feltwell (RAFF) in the United Kingdom. Purpose of Market Research: Our primary objective is to gain an understanding of how the Government's required delivery outcome can be achieved at a reasonable/sustainable cost while also being reliable. The Government is not seeking an unnecessarily complex or premium delivery model where a simpler commercial solution could reliably satisfy the requirement. *This RFI is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or promise to issue a future solicitation. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparation or submission of information in response to this RFI. * Background: Personnel who live or work on RAFL, RAFM, and RAF Feltwell receive both personal and official parcels from commercial delivery companies. The most common carriers, presently, have been DPD, DHL, Evri, FedEx, Parcelforce, UPS, Amazon, and Royal Mail. Royal Mail/Parcelforce are the only delivery entities that presently have installation access and deliver directly to the on-base addresses. Other commercial parcel delivery companies do not have installation access, creating challenges in completing delivery to the intended on-base residence or agency. The Government is exploring a recurring parcel delivery service capable of receiving or otherwise obtaining parcels from commercial carriers that do not have installation access and completing final delivery to the intended residence or agency on RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall, or RAF Feltwell. The Government seeks industry�s recommendations regarding the most efficient and economical means of accomplishing this outcome. Packages, after they are picked up by a neighbor, have an average dwell time of 2 weeks before the intended recipients of the packages become aware that a neighbor had received their package on their behalf. The Government is particularly interested in solutions that make use of existing commercial capabilities and minimize unnecessary Government-specific processes, facilities, equipment, or infrastructure. Primary Constraints: Installation access and funding will be the primary constraints and will be the biggest factors considered in developing the desired solution. Presently installation access for local nationals can take upwards of 7 months due to the MOD clearance/background check process. The government is not aware of any route to expedite the processing of packages. It has been observed that the delivery driver experiences a high level of turnover, unpredictable routes for drivers, and criminal records that prohibit access to the installation which affects the parcel delivery companies� ability to obtain installation access for their drivers. Drones are not permitted on or near these installations and should not be included in identified solutions. Government-provided escorts will not be available as an interim staffing or access solution. Respondents should consider these conditions when describing their proposed solution and should identify how they could achieve the required staffing and access capability within the anticipated transition period. Respondents should also identify cost-effective approaches for maintaining sufficient access-qualified staffing without unnecessarily increasing the number of personnel requiring installation access. Estimated Parcel Volume: Available information indicates that approximately 1,000 parcels per week are associated with RAF Lakenheath that are being coordinated for pick-up at businesses near the installation. Should a reliable delivery service be established, the volume of parcels is expected to at least triple. Comparable parcel-volume information is not currently available for RAFM or RAFF. The bases in order of highest estimated volume to lowest are as follows: RAFL, RAFF, RAFM. All quantities provided in this RFI are estimates for market research and planning purposes and should not be interpreted as guaranteed quantities or maximum quantities. Suggested solutions will need to be scalable to fluctuate as personnel to the bases fluctuate and parcel volume fluctuates. Respondents should identify how uncertainty and fluctuations in parcel volume would affect their recommended solution and pricing. Respondents are also encouraged to suggest a Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) structure best suited to their recommendation. Respondents are specifically encouraged to identify approaches that allow the service to scale efficiently as parcel volume changes without requiring the Government to pay for unnecessary excess capacity during lower-volume periods. Desired Outcome: The desired outcome is a reliable and cost-effective service capable of delivering eligible parcels from commercial delivery companies that do not have installation access to the residence or agency on the installation that ordered the item. The service would be expected to support RAFL, RAFM, and RAFF. All three installations are anticipated to be included from the very beginning of performance. The service would handle both personal and official parcels. Delivery service is expected seven days per week. For residential deliveries, parcels that do not require a recipient signature may be left at the recipient's door (or in a safe place designated by their delivery notes). The Government recognizes that commercial carriers may transfer parcels at different times throughout the day. Respondents should identify any operational assumptions, carrier coordination, cutoff times, or other conditions necessary to accomplish daily delivery. Solutions should not be disruptive, so the preference is to find a solution to deliver packages by 1700 each day ensuring no nighttime disruptions. If a requirement or assumption described in this RFI would have a significant impact on the cost, please identify the cost driver and recommend a less expensive alternative that would still provide reliable on-base parcel delivery. Commercial Carrier Coordination The Government has not established the required method for obtaining parcels from commercial carriers that lack installation access. Respondents should recommend solutions. If multiple solutions are available, you are encouraged to make multiple recommendations. The Government is interested in understanding how industry could establish effective and economical means of accepting, collecting, transferring, consolidating, or otherwise obtaining custody of eligible parcels from commercial delivery companies and subsequently completing final delivery to the appropriate on-base residence or agency. The Government has not determined whether an on-base facility, off-base facility, consolidation point, direct carrier transfer, existing commercial facility, existing delivery network, or another method represents the most effective solution. Respondents should identify the approach they recommend and any Government support, facilities, infrastructure, or coordination that would be necessary for that approach. *There is a preference for practical solutions leveraging existing commercial operations, avoiding the creation of dedicated infrastructure where it is not necessary to achieve the required outcome. * Package Manifest/Security Information Packages entering the installations must be supported by appropriate manifest information or a form of documentation of items being transported/number of packages being delivered. Ideally, security forces would have visibility of the items contained within individual packages when

title: Technology Licensing Opportunity: Room-Temperature Electrochemical Metallization of Rare Earth Elements
description: Note: This is a technology licensing opportunity. No procurement, grants, or funding opportunities are associated with this notice. Room-Temperature Electrochemical Metallization of Rare Earth Elements A low-energy, low-hazard alternative to molten-salt electrolysis for sustainable REE production. Technology Summary This invention introduces a method to produce metallic rare earth elements (REEs) through room-temperature electrometallization in anhydrous electrolytes. By leveraging unique ion-pairing interactions, Lewis acid-base chemistry, and interfacial structuring, the system enables efficient REE reduction and stable metal formation without the extreme energy use or toxic byproducts of conventional fused salt electrolysis. Problem Addressed High cost & regulatory barriers: Current molten-salt electrolysis (600�1200 �C) generates toxic HF gas and rare earth fluoride waste, triggering costly EPA and OSHA compliance requirements. Environmental impact: Legacy processes produce hazardous waste with long-term contamination risks, leading to industry abandonment in North America. Supply chain dependence: Metallic REEs are only produced at scale in China, creating vulnerabilities for U.S. manufacturers and defense applications. Solution The invention replaces high-temperature fused salt electrolysis with an ambient-temperature electrochemical process. The approach integrates three synergistic innovations: Tuned electrolyte nucleophilicity � enabling more efficient reduction pathways. Lewis acid-base coordination control � stabilizing the ligand environment during deposition. Interfacial electrochemical structuring � improving reaction kinetics and metal stability. This combination allows REE electrodeposition at room temperature, reducing both energy demand and hazardous byproduct formation. This invention enables dual functionality, electrodeposition and (in-situ) electrorefining. Key Advantages Lower energy consumption � eliminates the need for 600�1200 �C molten salt processes. Reduced environmental liabilities � avoids HF gas emissions and toxic fluoride salt accumulation. Safer operations � circumvents EPA and RCRA compliance barriers tied to FSE. Domestic supply potential � enables North American REE production for critical industries. Scalable platform � adaptable to multiple REEs including neodymium, samarium, dysprosium, and terbium. Market Applications Permanent magnets � essential for EV traction motors, wind turbines, and energy-efficient refrigeration. Defense systems � critical components for satellites, communication devices, and advanced weapons. Lightweight alloys � enhancing aerospace and automotive materials. Electronics � miniaturized devices requiring REE-based components. Battery technologies � advanced REE-containing chemistries for high-performance storage.

description: ****SOURCES SOUGHT FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY**** This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this announcement. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 1. AGENCY: United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) 2. NAICS: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction 3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Peru 4. ACQUISITION INFORMATION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA), is issuing this Sources Sought announcement as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support a potential future design-build construction project at the Callao Naval Base, Lima, Peru. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. Estimated Magnitude of Construction: Between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000. Performance Period: 540 days after Notice to Proceed. Anticipated Award Date: Fiscal Year 2027 Quarter 3 Small Business Programs: In accordance with FAR 19.000(b)(1)(ii), the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) has elected not to apply FAR Part 19 (Small Business Programs) to this overseas procurement. Consequently, small business set-asides will not be utilized for this project in Peru. However, all responsible sources�including both U.S. concerns (large and small) and foreign entities�are encouraged to submit responses to this Sources Sought notice. 5. ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: The acquisition strategy for this requirement will be determined based on the responses to this Sources Sought notice and other market research. The Government is considering several compliant acquisition pathways to ensure the successful delivery of this complex Design-Build project in Peru. All interested firms are strongly encouraged to submit a comprehensive capabilities statement, as the information received will be critical in determining the final method of procurement. The primary anticipated strategy is a Two-Phase Design-Build procurement under the authority of FAR Part 36.3. In this scenario, the Government would issue a public Phase 1 solicitation requesting offeror qualifications. Based on these qualifications, the Government would down-select the most highly qualified firms (typically no more than five) who would then be eligible to compete in Phase 2 and submit detailed technical and price proposals. However, based on the unique challenges of performing complex construction in Peru, the Government is also considering the following alternative strategies: Option 1: Limited Competition under FAR Part 6, Other Than Full and Open Competition. If market research reveals that only a very limited number of sources possess the unique combination of Design-Build expertise, mandatory Peruvian licensing (Registro Nacional de Proveedores - RNP), and demonstrated experience with specialized facilities (e.g., POL, medical, secure warehouses) in the local market, the Government may justify limiting competition. Option 2: Establishment of a Qualified Bidders List (QBL) under FAR Part 9.2. If the operational environment in Peru and the specialized nature of the requirement warrant it, the Government may decide to establish a formal Qualification Requirement. Under this authority, the Government would create a list of pre-qualified firms that demonstrate the essential standards for technical capability, financial stability, and in-country operational capacity. Future solicitations for this requirement would then be limited to firms on this established QBL. The Government�s final decision will be based on which strategy provides the best value and ensures a competitive environment among responsible and qualified contractors capable of meeting the demanding technical and logistical requirements of this project. 6. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The contemplated scope consists of complete Design-Build services�including geotechnical verification, site preparation, civil works, architectural and engineering design after award, structural construction, mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP), specialized HVAC/fire suppression, Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance coverage, and Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E). Facility / Scope Package Primary Function Key Technical Considerations Building 110 Spare Parts Warehouse Heavy-duty slab design, industrial racking integration, material handling flow, automated logistics staging. Building 115 Clothing & Gear Warehouse High-density pallet storage, humidity and climate control, inventory distribution bays. Building 112 Material Warehouse Bulk staging, overhead crane/hoist accommodations, heavy equipment ingress/egress ramps. Building 113 Customs Warehouse Secure bonded holding areas, host-nation customs inspection layout, physical security infrastructure. Building 114 Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) Warehouse Secondary containment, explosion-proof electrical systems, specialized foam/water fire suppression, environmental drainage controls. Building 111 Medicine & Medical Supplies Warehouse Temperature/humidity-controlled storage (cold chain capability), pharmaceutical-grade clean finishings, backup power integration. Building 120 DIRNOTEMAT & Quality Control Building Administrative offices, testing and quality inspection laboratories, specialized testing benches, IT/telecom infrastructure. Site & Ancillary Works Infrastructure & Integration Site grading, structural fill, perimeter security, access roads, utility connections, complete FF&E packages, and host-nation compliant permitting. 7. SOURCES SOUGHT: The purpose of this source sought is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of contractors who have the capabilities to complete and perform contracts of this magnitude, and to address any questions, recommendations or concerns from Industry. The Government must ensure there is adequate competition among potential pool of responsible contractors. Prior Government contract work is not required for submitting a response under this Sources Sought announcement. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. 8. title: Henkilöstön osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut 2027-2029 (2030)
description: Henkilöstön osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut 2027-2029 (2030) Hankinnan kohteena on Jyväskylän kaupungin henkilöstöön kuuluvien esimiesten ja työyhteisöjen osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, sillä jakaminen ei palvelun luonteen vuoksi ole tarkoituksenmukaista eikä jaosta saada selkeää. Sen sijaan poolista tehdään melko suuri, jotta saadaan laaja-alainen asiantuntijuus turvattua. Palveluiden hankinta voidaan toteuttaa joko henkilöstöhallinnon tai työyksiköiden esimiesten hankkimana tilanteissa, joissa on havaittu kehittämistarvetta. Tuleva hankinta koskee kaikkia Jyväskylän kaupungin toimialoja ja liikelaitoksia. Tarjouskilpailulla muodostetaan 15 yrityksen/toimijan pooli, tai useamman, mikäli mukaan ei saada vähintään 25 valmentajaa. Jos soveltuvia tarjouksia on vähemmän kuin 15, valitaan kaikki soveltuvat tarjoukset. Jotta turvataan pientenkin toimijoiden pääseminen hankintaan mukaan, rinnakkaisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä, ja yksi yritys/toimija voi tarjota 1-3 asiantuntijaa pooliin. Palvelun käynnistämisen tavoiteaika on 1.3.2027. Lisätiedot hankinnan kohteesta tarjouspyynnöstä ja sen liitteistä.,

title: Evaluering- Operativt SaLTo
description: Bydel Alna har behov for ekstern bistand til evaluering av prosjektet Operativt SaLTo. Prosjektet dreier seg om å finne nye metoder for å motvirke og forebygge ungdomskriminalitet. Evalueringen skal gi et faglig og operativt beslutningsgrunnlag for videreutvikling, videreføring og eventuell implementering av prosjektets samarbeidsmodell og arbeidsmetodikk. Oppdraget skal belyse hvordan modellen fungerer i praksis, identifisere hvilke deler som bør videreføres, justeres eller avsluttes, og vurdere organisatoriske forutsetninger for videreføring. Et særskilt formål er å vurdere hvordan erfaringer, metoder og arbeidsformer fra prosjektet kan tas i bruk i ny organisasjon etter bydelsreform fra 2028. Estimert verdi på anskaffelsen er 700 000 kroner ekskl. mva.

title: Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) Modeling & Simulation Support
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is being issued by the Department of the Army, on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires. PAE Fires is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify qualified, experienced, and interested sources capable of providing specialized engineering, modeling, simulation, and software support for the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) Project Office in support of the AN/TPY-2 Terminal Mode. title: Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity-Multiple Award Contracts (IDIQ-MACs) at Mid-Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center (MARMC) for Next Generation Homeport CNO Availabilities
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N6117727R5001 for the award of the Mid-Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center (MARMC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity Multiple Award Contracts (IDIQ-MACs) for Continuous Maintenance Availabilities (CMAVs), Emergent Maintenance (EM), and short-term Chief of Naval Operations (CNO) availabilities. This solicitation is for the procurement of maintenance, repair and modernization of non-nuclear surface ships (including Guided-Missile Cruisers (CGs), Guided Missile Destroyers (DDGs), Expeditionary Sea Bases (ESBs), Guided-Missile Frigates (FFGs), Amphibious Command Ships (LCCs), Littoral Combat Ships (LCSs), Landing Helicopter Assaults (LHAs), Landing Helicopter Docks (LHDs), Landing Platform Docks (LPDs), Landing Ship Docks (LSDs), and Mine Countermeasures Ships (MCMs) homeported in or visiting the Norfolk region. PAEM intends to award IDIQ-MACs based on the qualifications and capabilities of the Contractor in the following two categories: MAC A, where all holders can complete all requirements; and MAC B, where all holders can complete work associated with CMAVs and EM on non-critical systems. MAC A will be solicited on a full and open basis. MAC B will be solicited as a Small Business Set Aide. MAC A � CMAV/EM includes work on critical systems. MAC A also includes short-term CNO availabilities. Due to the nature of critical systems and the likelihood of urgent requirements with critical EM, the Government will require contractors with the capability and capacity to respond immediately to critical technical requirements. It is anticipated that this work would be available under full and open competition. However, if it is determined that two or more small businesses are interested and capable of completing the scope of work under any given delivery order, contracting officers may use their discretion to restrict competition to small businesses. MAC B � CMAV/EM does not include work on critical systems but will include systems and equipment requiring work certification. The scope of non-critical contract actions is expected to require less contractor capabilities, both in human resources and facilities. MAC B will be a small business set aside. In the event that there is no interest expressed for any given delivery order, this work may be competed under MAC A. Offerors must possess or have the ability to obtain a Tier I, II, or III Master Ship Repair Agreement (MSRA) for the Norfolk, VA homeport. Each contract will include five (5) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. The solicitation will be issued electronically via System for Award Management (SAM) at http://sam.gov and interested parties must comply with that announcement. Interested offerors should monitor the SAM.gov page for any applicable amendments to this solicitation. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management in order to participate in this procurement at https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM/. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which shall be considered by the agency. SAM.gov is the single point of entry for posting of the synopsis and solicitations to the internet. This pre-solicitation notice is for information purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to solicit contractual offers or award of contracts. The Government is not soliciting, nor will it accept, proposals as a result of this synopsis. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or information provided as a result of this notice. The solicitation is forthcoming.

description: Der ZVH schreibt die Planung, Lieferung, Montage, Inbetriebnahme und betriebsfertige Übergabe einer Abluftreinigung aus. title: Greece, Lithuania, Poland, Cyprus – Research and experimental development services – Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP)
description: The Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP) project addresses critical gaps in personal protective equipment (PPE). It responds to the need to keep first responders safe and operationally effective during evolving threats, from CBRN incidents and HAZMAT situations to terrorism, industrial accidents, natural disasters, and other complex emergencies. ACTIVE PCP involves public safety buyers and end-users in defining unmet needs and guiding industry R&D towards solutions. ACTIVE PCP procures R&D services through Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP). // Tenderers are invited to propose innovative PPE solutions for first responders, police, firefighters, and emergency medical services operating in complex CBRN and HAZMAT environments. Following the phased PCP model, the procurement supports R&D up to the development of a limited volume of first products. It comprises 3 competitive Phases, with fewer Tenderers progressing at each stage so that those offering the strongest response to the PCP's technical challenge are selected. // The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement (FA) with call-offs for specific contracts for each of the 3 R&D phases (altogether ‘Contracts’). Greek law governs the Contracts. The GDPR Processing Agreement – if applicable – will be governed by the law of the Member State in which each pilot will take place during Phase 3. The FA will remain binding for the duration of all phases for which Contractors remain in the PCP. There will be no renegotiations. // KEMEA will be the Lead Procurer throughout all the phases of ACTIVE PCP. // Tenderers that are awarded a FA will also be awarded a specific contract for Phase 1 (evaluation of tenders for the FA and Phase 1 are combined). Tenderers are therefore asked not only to submit their detailed offer for Phase 1, but also to state their goals, and to outline their plans (including price conditions) for Phases 2 and 3. // The three Phases are: (i) Phase 1: Solution Design. A FA and a Specific Contract for Phase 1 will be awarded to at least six (6) contractors; (ii) Phase 2: Prototyping. A call-off will be organised for Phase 2, with the aim of awarding at least three (3) Phase 2 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 1 will be eligible for Phase 2. The procurers will validate the Phase 2 prototypes; and (iii) Phase 3: Original development and testing. A second call-off will be organised for Phase 3, with the aim of awarding a minimum of two (2) Phase 3 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 2 will be eligible for Phase 3. The procurers will validate the Phase 3 prototypes. // Offers for the next phase will be requested together with the End of Phase deliverables of the previous phase. I.e., all Contractors of the previous phase have the right to submit offers for the next phase (together with their End of Phase Report). A Contractor must have been awarded a Specific Contract for Phase 1 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 2. Likewise, a Contractor must have been awarded Specific Contracts for Phases 1 and 2 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 3. The maximum total budget for this PCP is 3.650.000 EUR including VAT, taxes and other related fees and costs). // The maximum budget per phase and the maximum budget per Contractor (excluding VAT, including taxes and other related fees and costs) are as follows: For Phase 1 (Solution Design): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €47,043.00; Total subcontracting cost for phase 1: €282,258.05. For Phase 2 (Prototyping): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €483,870.97; Total subcontracting cost for phase 2: €1,451,612.90. For Phase 3 (Original development and testing): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €604,838.71; Total subcontracting cost for phase 3: €1,209,677.42. For Phase 1, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of Tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 2, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best Tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 3, contracts for Phase 3 will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // As leftover budget from the previous phase can be transferred to the next phase(s), the total budget available for Phases 2 and/or 3 may eventually be higher than stated here (but the maximum budget per Contractor for Phases 2 and 3 will remain the same). // Further information on ACTIVE PCP as well as the Tender Documents can be found at https://www.activepcp.eu/
